gaps.sentence: You ___ have left the door unlocked — anyone could have walked in.
gaps.explanation: 'Shouldn't have' blames someone for a past act: shouldn't have.

gaps.sentence: You ___ use my office while I am on holiday.
The theatre was completely empty, so the performance ___ have been very popular.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' draws a negative conclusion from evidence: can't have been.

gaps.sentence: It is Saturday tomorrow, so I ___ get up early.
gaps.hint: an absence of obligation at weekends
gaps.explanation: 'Don't have to' shows there is no obligation: don't have to get up.

gaps.sentence: Candidates ___ switch off their phones before the exam begins.
He ___ have missed the train — he left home two hours early.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' expresses near-certainty that something did not happen: can't have missed.

gaps.sentence: You ___ as well take the early train — the later one is often cancelled.
gaps.hint: might as well = no reason not to
gaps.explanation: 'Might as well' suggests an option because the alternative is worse.

gaps.sentence: When the lift broke, I ___ walk up ten flights of stairs.
gaps.hint: necessity created by a past event
gaps.explanation: 'Had to' expresses past necessity: had to walk.
